items.name: Big Buddha
items.nameThai: พระพุทธมิ่งมงคลเอกนาคคีรี
items.coordSource: google-maps-listing+wikipedia+osm
items.gmapsQuery: Phuket Big Buddha, Chalong, Phuket
items.bestTime: Just after the 9:00 opening: cool air and few people. No sunset here, the gate closes at 18:00.
items.openText: Daily 9:00-18:00, last entry 17:30 (two 2026 guides; Google Maps still shows 6:00-18:30). Open again since 3 March 2026.
items.feeText: Free. Donations welcome. Parking and sarongs are free.
items.gettingThere: Hill road from Chaofa West Road (signs from Chalong Circle). Car or scooter: about 35-45 min from Patong, 20-25 min from Kata. Grab and Bolt drive to the top; book the ride back from the car park.
items.description: A 45 m white marble Buddha on top of Nakkerd Hill. It closed after a landslide in August 2024 and reopened on 3 March 2026. The terrace has wide views over Kata, Karon and Chalong Bay. It is an active temple, so dress and behave with respect.
tips: Cover shoulders and knees. Free sarongs at the entrance.
Sunset is about 18:25 in January, after closing time. Watch it from Nak-Kerd Seaview Cafe on the road down (open to 20:00).
The road down is steep with tight bends. Ride slowly on a scooter.
Only the statue, main stairs, temple area and terraces are open. Follow the signs and barriers.
After heavy rain, check that it is open before you go. Access rules have changed several times since 2024.
items.verification: Checked 15 Oct 2026. Reopening on 3 Mar 2026, free entry and 9:00-18:00 (last entry 17:30) confirmed in Phuket 101 (updated 13 Oct 2026) and Window on Phuket (2026). Google Maps lists 6:00-18:30 (4.6 stars, 39,700 reviews), so I kept the stricter guide hours. Only a 15-rai area is open, under 25 Forestry Department conditions. Coords: Google listing, Wikipedia (7.827598, 98.312853) and OSM agree within 20 m.

items.name: Wat Chalong
items.nameThai: วัดฉลอง (วัดไชยธาราราม)
items.coordSource: google-maps-listing+wikipedia+osm
items.gmapsQuery: Wat Chalong, Chalong, Phuket
items.bestTime: Early morning, about 8:00-9:30, before the heat and the tour buses.
items.openText: Temple buildings daily from 7:00 or 8:00 to 17:00 (sources differ). You can walk the grounds outside these hours.
items.feeText: Free. Donations welcome. Free parking.
items.gettingThere: On Chaofa West Road near Chalong Circle. Car or scooter: about 30-40 min from Patong, 15-20 min from Kata. About 15 min by car from the Big Buddha.
items.description: Phuket's largest and most important Buddhist temple. Climb the 60 m Grand Pagoda: the lower floors have Buddha statues and murals, and the top floor holds a small bone relic of the Buddha. Loud firecrackers are normal: locals light them to give thanks when a wish comes true.
tips: No shorts or short skirts, no sleeveless tops. Take off shoes and hats before you enter a building.
Speak quietly and do not touch the statues.
Easy to combine with the Big Buddha and The Distillery Phuket (Chalong Bay Rum) in one trip.
items.verification: Checked 15 Oct 2026. Free entry, free parking and 7:00-17:00 in Phuket 101 (updated 12 Jul 2026) and the temple FAQ site. Google Maps lists 8:00-17:00, so the best time now starts at 8:00. The 60 m chedi with a Buddha relic is confirmed by Phuket 101 and the temple site. Big Buddha to Wat Chalong is 7.7 km (OSRM). Coords: Google listing (44 m), Wikipedia (23 m) and OSM temple area agree.

items.name: Phuket Old Town
items.nameThai: เมืองเก่าภูเก็ต
items.coordSource: osm(Soi Rommanee way)+google-maps(Soi Rommani)+wikipedia
items.gmapsQuery: Soi Rommani, Phuket Old Town
items.bestTime: Early morning (8:00-10:00) for empty streets and soft light, or late afternoon. On Sunday, stay for the night market.
items.openText: Public streets, always open. Shop and cafe hours vary.
items.feeText: Free to walk. Thai Hua Museum: 200 THB, plus 200 THB if you want to take photos inside.
items.gettingThere: Car or Grab: about 25-35 min from Patong (over Patong Hill), 30-40 min from Kata. Parking in the old streets is hard, so Grab is easier.
items.description: The historic center of Phuket Town. Colorful Sino-Portuguese shophouses from the tin-mining era line Thalang, Dibuk, Krabi and Phang Nga roads. Soi Romanee is the prettiest small lane. Come for cafes, street art, Chinese shrines and local food such as Hokkien noodles.
tips: Thai Hua Museum (28 Krabi Rd) explains Phuket's Chinese history, 9:00-17:00. Sources differ on its closed day (Monday, Wednesday, or none on Google), so Sunday is a safe choice.
It is hot by 11:00. Walk early, then rest in a cafe.
On Sunday 10 or 17 Jan, stay for the Lard Yai walking street market.
End the day at Khao Rang Viewpoint for sunset, about 5 min by car.
items.verification: Checked 15 Oct 2026. Thai Hua Museum: 200 THB plus a 200 THB photo pass (Phuket 101, updated 26 Sep 2026, and other listings). The closed day conflicts: Phuket 101 says Monday, a July 2026 listing says Wednesday, Google lists 9:00-17:00 daily. Coords: OSM Soi Rommanee way and Google 'Soi Rommani' within 10 m; Wikipedia Old Town point 180 m west. I changed gmapsQuery because 'Soi Romanee' first finds a bakery with that name.

items.name: Sunday Walking Street Market (Lard Yai)
items.nameThai: ถนนคนเดิน หลาดใหญ่
items.coordSource: osm-market-way+google-maps-listing
items.gmapsQuery: Lard Yai Sunday Night Market, Thalang Road, Phuket Town
items.bestTime: Arrive 16:30-17:00. By 19:00-20:00 it is very crowded.
items.openText: Sundays only, about 16:00-22:00 (Google says to 23:00). On your trip: Sun 10, 17 and 24 Jan 2027.
items.feeText: Free entry. Bring small cash notes.
items.gettingThere: Grab or taxi from Patong about 25-30 min (about 300-500 THB, check the app), from Kata 30-40 min. Do not drive: parking near Thalang Road is very hard on Sundays.
items.description: Every Sunday evening, Thalang Road in the Old Town closes to cars and becomes a 360 m street market. Stalls sell Phuket snacks, handmade crafts and clothes, with music and street shows. It is busy and local, and the old shophouses make a great backdrop.
tips: Try Phuket snacks like o-tao, a-pong and Hokkien noodles.
Most stalls take cash only; some take Thai QR payment.
Walk the street in one direction and leave at the other end. Turning back in the crowd is slow.
Come earlier and see the Old Town in daylight first.
items.verification: Checked 15 Oct 2026. Sunday about 16:00-22:00 in Window on Phuket, 21 Sensations (5 Apr 2026) and Thai Holiday Guide (Jul 2026). Google lists Sun 16:00-23:00 (4.5 stars, 2,250 reviews). No 2026 reports of a move or pause. OSM opening_hours tag (18:00) is outdated. Coords: OSM market way (3 m) and Google listing (110 m east) agree. Grab price 300-500 THB from one guide (goasia.cc).

items.name: Promthep Cape
items.nameThai: แหลมพรหมเทพ
items.coordSource: osm-viewpoint+osm-lighthouse+google-maps-listing
items.gmapsQuery: Promthep Cape, Rawai, Phuket
items.bestTime: Sunset, about 18:25 in January. Arrive by 17:30 for parking and a good spot.
items.openText: Open 24 hours. The lighthouse museum has shorter hours (about 9:00-17:00 or 18:00, sources differ).
items.feeText: Free. Free parking. The small lighthouse museum is free.
items.gettingThere: Southern tip of the island, past Nai Harn. Car or scooter: about 35-45 min from Patong, 15-20 min from Kata. Traffic is slow right after sunset.
items.description: The southern tip of Phuket and the island's most famous sunset point. Terraces look west over the sea and small islands. Next to the white lighthouse (with a small free museum) is a Brahma shrine surrounded by hundreds of elephant statues. Expect big crowds at sunset.
tips: Tour buses arrive around 17:00-18:00. Come early, or stay 20 min after sunset when most people leave.
The lighthouse museum may close before sunset. Come earlier if you want to see it.
A rough path goes down to the tip of the cape. Wear shoes, take water and come back before dark.
Less crowded option: Windmill Viewpoint, about 1.3 km north by road.
Respect the shrine and do not touch the offerings.
items.verification: Checked 15 Oct 2026. Open 24 h, free entry and parking per Phuket 101 (updated 5 Aug 2026). Google also lists 24 h (4.7 stars, 18,900 reviews). Museum hours conflict between listings. No sign that the planned skywalk (a 2022 plan) is being built. Coords: OSM sunset viewpoint node, OSM lighthouse museum and Google's 'Promthep Cape' scenic-spot listing are all within 30 m, so I raised confidence to high. An older Google pin sits at the rocky tip, 360 m SW.

items.name: Windmill Viewpoint
items.coordSource: google-maps-listing+osm
items.gmapsQuery: Windmill Viewpoint, Nai Harn, Phuket
items.bestTime: Late afternoon to sunset (about 18:25 in January). Calmer than Promthep Cape.
items.openText: Open hilltop by the road. Google lists it as open 24 hours; a Feb 2026 news report says daily 6:00-19:00.
items.feeText: Free.
items.gettingThere: On the road from Nai Harn to Promthep Cape: after the lake, go up the hill to a sharp left bend and take the short dirt track. About 30-40 min from Patong, 15-20 min from Kata.
items.description: A grassy hilltop next to a large wind turbine, between Nai Harn and Promthep Cape. You look down on small Ya Nui Beach and Koh Man island, with Promthep in the distance. There is a little parking, a shade pavilion and a drinks stall. A calm sunset choice.
tips: Little shade: bring water and a hat in the daytime.
The access road is narrow and steep, and the car park is small. A scooter or taxi is easier than a big car.
Do Karon Viewpoint, Nai Harn, Windmill and Promthep in one afternoon loop.
On clear days you may see paragliders over Ya Nui Beach.
items.verification: Checked 15 Oct 2026. Free entry in Pattaya Mail (23 Feb 2026: daily 6:00-19:00, inside EGAT's Promthep energy station) and Thai Holiday Guide (updated Oct 2026: open roadside lookout, no gate). Google lists 24 h (4.7 stars, 6,500 reviews). I removed the pre-wedding photo tip because I found no source for it. Coords: Google listing and OSM viewpoint within 40 m.

items.name: Black Rock Viewpoint (Pa Hin Dam)
items.nameThai: ผาหินดำ
items.coordSource: google-maps-listing+osm
items.gmapsQuery: Black Rock Viewpoint, Karon, Phuket
items.bestTime: Early morning or late afternoon. Midday is very hot. Start down before dark (sunset about 18:25).
items.openText: Open hillside, no gate.
items.feeText: Free. No source reports a fee for the viewpoint.
items.gettingThere: From Karon Viewpoint drive toward Nai Harn and take the second road on the right (sign 'Nui Beach'). After about 1 km of dirt road, keep left at the fork (Thai sign ผาหินดำ). About 500 m later, park at the rock painted 'PA HIN DUM' and walk up about 10 min. About 15-25 min from Kata, 40-50 min from Patong.
items.description: One of the best views in south Phuket. From a rocky hilltop about 290 m high you see Nai Harn Bay, Ao Sane, Koh Man and Promthep Cape. Getting there takes effort: a bumpy dirt road, then a short, steep forest path. Few people, no shops, no railings.
tips: Wear sneakers, not flip-flops. The path is steep and loose in places.
A scooter handles the dirt road better than a car. Skip it after heavy rain.
There are no railings at the top. Stay away from the cliff edge.
Bring water; there is nothing to buy at the top.
There are no lights on the trail. Start down before it gets dark.
items.verification: Checked 15 Oct 2026. Route, 290 m height, 10 min walk and no railings come from Jamie's Phuket Blog (2017) and Phuket 101 (updated Feb 2025). Google lists it open 24 h (4.8 stars, 930 reviews). I removed the claim that Nui Beach charges entry: in May 2026 the government ordered Nui Beach land reclaimed and public access restored (Pattaya Mail, 15 May 2026). Road condition for 2027 is not confirmed. The image shows the bays from a high point, but the exact camera spot is not confirmed. Coords: Google listing and OSM viewpoint within 15 m.

items.name: Karon Viewpoint
items.coordSource: google-maps-listing+osm
items.gmapsQuery: Karon Viewpoint, Karon, Phuket
items.bestTime: 16:00-17:00 for warm light, or early morning for clear air. Midday light is flat.
items.openText: Open 24 hours.
items.feeText: Free. Free parking.
items.gettingThere: On the coast road from Kata Noi to Nai Harn. About 5-10 min from Kata, 25-30 min from Patong.
items.description: Phuket's classic postcard view: three bays in a row. Kata Noi is below, then Kata with little Koh Pu island, and Karon further north. A quick 15-minute stop with a large car park and small drink stalls, on the way to Nai Harn and Promthep Cape.
tips: The car park fills in the late afternoon in high season. Arrive before 16:00.
The dirt road to Black Rock Viewpoint starts a short drive south of here, toward Nai Harn.
Drinks and snacks are sold a few steps below the platform.
items.verification: Checked 15 Oct 2026. Free entry, open 24 h, large free car park and a 5-15 min stay per Phuket 101 (updated 23 Mar 2026). Google lists it open 24 h as 'Karon Viewpoint Phuket' (4.6 stars, 14,700 reviews). No 2026 reports of works or a fee. Coords: Google listing and OSM viewpoint within 10 m.

items.name: Kata Beach
items.nameThai: หาดกะตะ
items.coordSource: google-maps-listing+osm-beach
items.gmapsQuery: Kata Beach, Karon, Phuket
items.bestTime: Morning for a calm swim. Sunset (about 18:25) with Koh Pu island in front.
items.openText: Always open.
items.feeText: Free. Sunbeds and umbrellas for rent (price varies). Beach massage from about 300 THB.
items.gettingThere: In Kata: walk. From Patong about 20-30 min by car, scooter or Grab.
items.description: A 1.5 km bay of soft sand with Koh Pu island in front. From December to April the sea is usually calm and clear, good for swimming. It is more relaxed than Patong, with shade trees, beach restaurants and massages. The south end is the liveliest in the evening.
tips: Always respect red flags. Rip currents can still happen.
Sunbeds use only a small part of the beach. Bring a towel if you do not want to rent.
For sunset drinks, walk to the south end, where Ska Bar sits on the rocks.
items.verification: Checked 15 Oct 2026. Facts from Phuket 101 (updated 5 Oct 2026): 1.5 km beach, calm Dec-Apr, massage from 300 THB, red flags, south end liveliest. Ska Bar is still on Google Maps at the south end (open 10:00-1:00). Coords: Google listing (45 m) and OSM beach centre (110 m).

items.name: Kata Noi Beach
items.nameThai: หาดกะตะน้อย
items.coordSource: google-maps-listing+osm-beach
items.gmapsQuery: Kata Noi Beach, Karon, Phuket
items.bestTime: Before 10:00: easier parking and shade at both ends.
items.openText: Always open.
items.feeText: Free. No public sunbed rental: sunbeds and umbrellas are only for guests of Katathani and The Shore.
items.gettingThere: About 5 min by car or 15-20 min on foot (hilly road) from Kata. 25-30 min from Patong. Small car park at the south end near Katathani, plus a few roadside spots.
items.description: A small, quieter bay just south of Kata, with soft white sand and clear water. In the dry season the sea is calm and good for swimming, and lifeguards work in the daytime. Most of the beachfront is taken by one big resort, Katathani, so there are few shops or bars.
tips: Bring a towel or mat and your own shade.
The middle of the beach has no shade after mid-morning. Sit near the trees at either end.
Karon Viewpoint is 5 min up the hill.
items.verification: Checked 15 Oct 2026. Phuket 101 (updated 16 Sep 2026; URL now redirects to /kata-noi-beach-phuket/) confirms: sunbeds only for Katathani and The Shore guests, daytime lifeguards, south-end car park, calm sea Nov-Apr. Walk from Kata south end is 1.1 km, about 15 min (OSRM). Coords: Google listing (23 m) and OSM beach (8 m).

items.name: Nai Harn Beach
items.nameThai: หาดในหาน
items.coordSource: google-maps-beach-listing+osm-beach
items.gmapsQuery: Nai Han Beach หาดในหาน, Rawai, Phuket
items.bestTime: Morning or late afternoon. December and January can be busy.
items.openText: Always open.
items.feeText: Free. Beach massage about 300 THB per hour.
items.gettingThere: Car or scooter: about 30-40 min from Patong, 15-20 min from Kata.
items.description: A wide, natural bay in the far south of the island. The land behind the sand is protected, so there are no buildings, only tall casuarina trees. The water is clear blue in high season. Simple Thai restaurants are across the small road, and a temple and lake are behind the beach.
tips: A stream from the lake crosses the south end of the beach. Your feet will get wet.
Good base for sunset: Windmill Viewpoint and Promthep Cape are each 5-10 min away by car.
For a sunset drink, try Reflections Rooftop Bar at The Nai Harn hotel (opens 17:00).
items.verification: Checked 15 Oct 2026. Facts from Phuket 101 (updated 15 Sep 2026): protected beach land, stream at the south end, massage 300 THB per hour, Reflections Rooftop at The Nai Harn (also on Google Maps, 17:00-22:00). Coords: Google beach listing and OSM beach within 35 m. I changed gmapsQuery because 'Nai Harn Beach, Rawai' opens a village pin about 900 m inland; the Thai name opens the beach itself.

items.name: Freedom Beach
items.coordSource: google-maps-listing+osm-beach
items.gmapsQuery: Freedom Beach, Karon, Phuket
items.bestTime: Morning on a calm day. Boats run mainly from December to May.
items.openText: Daytime only. Boat access is mainly December-May.
items.feeText: Longtail from Patong: about 1,000-1,500 THB return per boat. Walk-in: free to 200 THB per person, depending on the path (sources differ). Scooter parking may cost about 100 THB.
items.gettingThere: Longtail boat from the south end of Patong Beach (near Amari), about 10 min. Or drive to The Lek Sand Beach Bar on the Patong-Karon hill road and hike down 15-25 min. The trailhead is about 15 min from Patong, 25 min from Kata.
items.description: A 300 m cove of soft white sand and clear water just south of Patong. You arrive by longtail boat or by a steep jungle trail, so it is much calmer than the big beaches. There is some snorkeling at both ends. Barefoot Bistro at the south end serves food and drinks.
tips: Agree the boat price and pickup time before you leave Patong.
There is no pier: you step off the boat into the water. Use a dry bag.
The hike back up is hard. Sometimes a 4x4 ride up costs about 100 THB per person.
Toilets and showers may be closed. Bring water, snorkel gear and real shoes for the trail.
items.verification: Checked 15 Oct 2026. The old note was wrong: North Abroad (updated 22 Sep 2026) does not give 200 THB. It says the Lek Sand path is free, another entrance costs about 100 THB, the boat is 1,000-1,500 THB, and the toilets were closed. Phuket 101 (updated 13 Aug 2026) says 200 THB walk-in and 1,200-1,500 THB by boat. Google names the trailhead 'The Lek Sand Beach Bar - Free Entrance to Freedom Beach'. Coords: Google listing and OSM beach within 55 m.

items.name: Patong Beach
items.nameThai: หาดป่าตอง
items.coordSource: google-maps-beach-listing+osm-beach
items.gmapsQuery: Patong Beach, Patong, Phuket
items.bestTime: Morning for a calmer swim; sunset from the sand. The north end is quieter all day.
items.openText: Always open.
items.feeText: Free. Sunbeds and umbrellas for rent.
items.gettingThere: In Patong: walk. From Kata about 20-30 min by car, scooter or Grab.
items.description: Phuket's busiest and most famous beach: 3 km of sand in front of the main party town. Expect jet skis, parasailing, vendors and crowds in the center. The north end is quieter, with softer sand and cleaner water. The south end has longtail boats to Freedom Beach.
tips: Smoking is banned on Patong Beach outside marked smoking areas. The fine can be up to 100,000 THB.
Some jet ski renters claim damage after the ride. Take photos of the jet ski before you start, or skip it.
For a quieter swim, go to the north end.
Beach clubs: Kudo and Barra Cuda in the center, Fuga at the north end.

links.label: TAT news: smoking ban on Thai beaches

items.verification: Checked 15 Oct 2026. The 3 km beach, quieter north end, south-end longtails and beach clubs come from Phuket 101 (updated 4 Oct 2026). Kudo, Barra Cuda and Fuga are all on Google Maps at those positions. Smoking ban (fine up to 100,000 THB or 1 year jail, smoking zones allowed) from TAT (Oct 2017); no later source says it was lifted. Coords: Google beach listing and OSM beach within 55 m. I changed gmapsQuery because 'Patong Beach, Kathu' opens the Patong town pin 700 m inland.

items.name: Bangla Road
items.nameThai: ถนนบางลา
items.coordSource: google-maps-listing+osm-street
items.gmapsQuery: Bangla Road, Patong, Phuket
items.bestTime: 19:00-21:00 to look around; after 22:00 for the full party.
items.openText: Pedestrian street every night from about 18:00. Licensed venues open to 4:00; small bars often close about 2:00.
items.feeText: Free to walk. Beer about 100-180 THB, cocktails 200-350 THB. Club entry varies.
items.gettingThere: In Patong: walk. From Kata about 20-30 min by Grab or taxi.
items.description: Patong's famous 400 m party street. Neon beer bars, go-go bars, live music bars and big clubs like Illuzion fill it every night. Loud, chaotic and worth seeing once. The music is mostly commercial EDM, hip-hop and cover bands, not underground techno.
tips: Ignore touts with show cards. They do not work for the bars.
Check menu prices before you order.
Bangla Street Food stays open late if you are hungry after midnight.
Keep your phone and wallet in a front pocket in the crowd.
items.verification: Checked 15 Oct 2026. Phuket 101 (updated 27 Jul 2026) gives the 400 m length, walking street from about 18:00, licensed venues to 4:00, prices and the touts warning. Legal 4:00 closing in Patong started in Dec 2023. Illuzion is operating (DJ Mag Top 100 Clubs 2026, Google listing at 31 Bangla Rd). Bangla Street Food is on Google Maps. Coords: Google street pin (6 m) and OSM street (30 m).

items.name: Khao Rang Viewpoint
items.nameThai: จุดชมวิวเขารัง
items.coordSource: google-maps-listing+osm-viewpoint
items.gmapsQuery: Khao Rang Viewpoint, Phuket Town
items.bestTime: Sunset (about 18:25 in January) and the 20 min after, when the town lights come on.
items.openText: Viewing deck: free, listed as open 24 hours. Tunk Ka Cafe: daily about 11:00-22:00.
items.feeText: Free. Tunk Ka Cafe mains about 80-180 THB.
items.gettingThere: A few minutes uphill from Phuket Old Town. About 25-35 min from Patong, 30-40 min from Kata.
items.description: A green hill right above Phuket Town. A viewing deck looks over the city, Chalong Bay and Cape Panwa. Hilltop restaurants such as Tunk Ka Cafe serve Thai food with the same view. A good end to an Old Town day, especially at sunset.
tips: Book a rail-side table at Tunk Ka Cafe by phone (081 892 6315) and arrive about 18:00.
Monkeys live near the top. Do not feed them and keep food in closed bags.
Phuket Old Town is about 5 min away by car.
items.verification: Checked 15 Oct 2026. Tunk Ka Cafe hours (11:15-22:00, Sat from 11:00) and phone come from Phuket 101 (updated 26 Sep 2026); Google lists 11:00-22:00 daily (4.4 stars, 1,900 reviews). Google lists the viewpoint as open 24 h; I found no 2026 closure or works. Views over town, Chalong Bay and Cape Panwa per Jamie's Phuket Blog; monkeys per Phuket 101 and Jamie's blog. Coords: Google listing (16 m) and OSM viewpoint (3 m).

items.name: Rawai Seafood Market
items.nameThai: ตลาดทะเลสด หาดราไวย์
items.coordSource: google-maps-place(cid 13174993957907334813)+osm-marketplace-way-142750664
items.gmapsQuery: Rawai Seafood Market, Rawai, Phuket
items.bestTime: Around 18:00-19:00 for dinner and a lively scene. Late morning is quietest.
items.openText: Daily. Google lists 9:00-21:00, Phuket 101 says 11:00-21:00. Mook Manee, the biggest restaurant, is open 11:30-22:00.
items.feeText: Seafood is priced per kg (large prawns up to about 1,500 THB/kg). Cooking fee about 100 THB per kg, or 50-100 THB per dish.
items.gettingThere: On Wiset Road next to Rawai Pier. About 35-45 min from Patong, 15-25 min from Kata.
items.description: A 100 m strip next to Rawai Pier, in an old sea gypsy fishing village. Fish stalls are on one side, restaurants on the other. You choose fish, prawns, crab or lobster, pay by weight, and a restaurant across the road cooks it your way. Fun, but no longer cheap.
tips: Agree the price per kg before they bag it, and watch the scale.
Ask the cooking fee first: some places charge per kg, others per dish.
Bring cash for the stalls.
Mook Manee, between the pier and the market, is the biggest restaurant here and is listed in the Michelin Guide.

imageCandidates.source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Phuket_-_Rawai_Beach_11.jpg (Rawai Beach next to the market; no free photo of the market itself found)

items.verification: Checked 15 Oct 2026. Phuket 101 (updated 21 Sep 2026): buy-and-cook system, cooking fees, prawns up to 1,500 THB/kg, 11:00-21:00. Google Maps listing active (4.4, 4,700+ reviews, 9:00-21:00 daily). Mook Manee on Google (11:30-22:00) and in the Michelin Guide. Pin 21 m from the Google place and 23 m from the OSM fish-market polygon. Guide links moved to sources (no official site).

items.name: Naka Weekend Market
items.coordSource: official-site-gmaps-link+google-maps-place+osm-marketplace-way-232288841
items.gmapsQuery: Naka Weekend Market, Wirat Hong Yok Road, Phuket
items.bestTime: Arrive 16:30-17:30, before the big evening crowd and the parking jam.
items.openText: Saturday and Sunday 16:00-22:00 (Google, Phuket 101 and the official site footer; the official home page says 23:00). On your trip: Sat 9, Sun 10, Sat 16, Sun 17, Sat 23 and Sun 24 Jan 2027. On weekdays only the street-food zone is open.
items.feeText: Free entry.
items.gettingThere: South edge of Phuket Town, near Central Phuket. About 20-30 min from Patong, 25-35 min from Kata. The car park at the back jams at night; roadside parking is often easier.
items.description: Phuket's biggest weekend night market, on the south edge of Phuket Town. Hundreds of stalls sell cheap clothes, souvenirs and gadgets, plus a large street-food area. There is live music on the stage in the evening. Busy, hot and very local.
tips: Bargain for clothes and souvenirs, but not for food.
Bring small cash notes.
Eat early, around 17:00, then shop when it cools down.
Local guitarist Nene Royal often plays the new stage at about 19:00 on market nights.
items.verification: Checked 15 Oct 2026. tips: Bring cash in small notes. Do not count on paying by phone.
On Fridays, get to the container bars early for an upstairs seat.
The quieter Retro Area at the back is good for a drink.

items.name: Nai Yang Beach (Sirinat National Park)
items.nameThai: หาดในยาง
items.coordSource: phuket101-page-geo+osm-beach-way-1020477061+commons-photo-gps
items.gmapsQuery: Nai Yang Beach, Sakhu, Thalang, Phuket
items.bestTime: Late afternoon: shade, plane landings and sunset (about 18:25-18:30). On your flight day, Tue 26 Jan, come in the late morning and leave by about 14:45.
items.openText: Beach always open. Sirinat National Park office: 8:00-16:30.
items.feeText: Village part of the beach: free. Sirinat National Park fee for foreigners: 200 THB adult, 100 THB child, charged in the park area.
items.gettingThere: 5-10 min from Phuket Airport. About 45-60 min from Patong, 60-75 min from Kata.
items.description: A quiet, shady bay inside Sirinat National Park, next to the airport. Small seafood restaurants and bars sit under the trees, and the sea is calm in high season. About 2.5 km north, at Mai Khao Beach, planes land low over the sand in the dry season.
tips: Plane spotting: the south end of Mai Khao Beach, best from late morning to about 14:00 (see its card).
Stay out of the airport safety zone under the approach path. No drones, lasers or flash: penalties are heavy.
Flight day, Tue 26 Jan: the terminal is only 5-10 minutes by car. Leave the beach by about 14:45 to be there by 15:20.
Lunch on the sand: Sea Almond (Google 4.4, 855 reviews), Phen's (4.3, 1,260) and The Good View. For a bigger Southern Thai meal, Natural Restaurant is 2.4 km inland (see its card).
With luggage on the last day, leave your bags at your hotel or at the AIRPORTELs counter in the terminal (150 baht per bag) before you go to the beach.

items.name: Bang Pae Waterfall (Khao Phra Thaeo)
items.nameThai: น้ำตกบางแป
items.coordSource: osm-gibbon-project-node+thaiholidayguide-pin+google-gibbon-project (park entrance and car park)
items.gmapsQuery: Bang Pae Waterfall, Pa Khlok, Thalang, Phuket
items.bestTime: Weekday morning, before 10:00. In January the water is lower than in the rainy season.
items.openText: Daily, daytime. Google and Thai Holiday Guide say 9:00-16:00; other sources say 8:00-17:00 or 8:00-18:00. Arrive before 15:00.
items.feeText: Park fee for foreigners: 200 THB adult, 100 THB child in most sources. Phuket 101's FAQ and some visitor reviews say 400/200 THB, so carry 400 THB per adult in cash. The same-day ticket is also valid at Ton Sai Waterfall.
items.gettingThere: Off Route 4027 on the east side of the island. About 40-50 min from Patong, 50-60 min from Kata. About 10 min from the Phuket Elephant Sanctuary office.
items.description: The largest waterfall on Phuket, inside the Khao Phra Thaeo rainforest reserve. A 10-15 minute jungle path follows the stream to the falls and rock pools. In January the flow is getting low, so think forest walk, not big waterfall. The Gibbon Rehabilitation Project is at the entrance.
tips: Gibbon project: visits only in booked sessions (1 hour at 10:30, 12:30 or 14:00, or 2.5 hours from 9:30). On days with no bookings it is closed. Book online first.
Wear shoes with grip. The rocks are slippery; do not jump from them.
Alcohol is not allowed in the park.
Ton Sai Waterfall (same ticket) is very small in the dry season.
items.verification: Checked 15 Oct 2026. items.name: Phuket Elephant Sanctuary
items.coordSource: official-site-gmaps-link+osm-office-node-5945513052
items.gmapsQuery: Phuket Elephant Sanctuary, Pa Khlok, Thalang, Phuket
items.bestTime: Morning program (about 9:30-13:00) is cooler. Book several days ahead in high season.
items.openText: Every day except 13 April. Half-day programs: morning about 9:30-13:00, afternoon about 13:30-17:00. Booking required, no walk-ins.
items.feeText: Half day: 3,000 THB per adult (age 13+). Child prices on the booking page. Shared hotel transfer can be added. Shorter Canopy Walkway Tour (1.5 hours) from 1,900 THB. Full day from 7,000 THB.
items.gettingThere: Meet at the sanctuary office in Paklok (this pin), or book the shared hotel pickup. Self-drive about 40-50 min from Patong, 45-60 min from Kata.
items.description: An ethical sanctuary for rescued and retired elephants. There is no riding, no bathing and, since 1 April 2026, no feeding. You watch the elephants roam, forage and bathe freely from forest trails and a long canopy walkway. Lunch is a vegetarian Thai buffet.
tips: Book online first. There is no public access to the sanctuary; every visit starts at the office.
Wear clothes that can get dirty. Rubber boots, raincoats and mosquito spray are provided.
The visit includes the elephant hospital, Phuket's first.
Combine with Bang Pae Waterfall, about 10 min away.
Google's pin for the sanctuary is about 650 m from the meeting office. Use 'Directions to the office'.
items.verification: Checked 15 Oct 2026 on the official site: half day 3,000 THB (13+), 3.5 hours, 9:30-13:00 or 13:30-17:00, meet at the Paklok office, no public access or drop-ins, feeding stopped 1 Apr 2026, Canopy Walkway Tour from 1,900 THB, full day from 7,000 THB. The 1-hour tour ends with a tasting and a mojito. The bar and restaurant in the sugarcane garden are good for dinner.
tips: Book on the official site before you go.
Photos are not allowed inside the distillery.
After the tasting, take Grab instead of riding a scooter.
Cocktail workshops start at 12:00 (vodka), 14:00 (rum) and 16:00 (gin).

items.name: Banana Beach

items.bestTime: Weekday morning, before 10:00. The sea is calm from November to April.
items.openText: Public beach, best in daylight.
items.feeText: Beach free. Parking 100 THB. Toilet and shower 20 THB. Sunbeds extra.
items.gettingThere: Car or scooter, on the coast road between Layan and Nai Thon. The car park is at the north end of the beach, between Trisara resort and Andaman White Beach Resort. Coming from Bang Tao, pass Trisara and turn left. Coming from Nai Thon, pass Andaman White Beach Resort and turn right. From the car park you are on the sand in one minute.
items.description: Small cove with soft sand, clear water and rocks for snorkelling at both ends. Late in 2025 the old jungle path closed. Now you park at a new car park at the north end, next to a new beach club with music. The old family restaurant further south is still open.
tips: Arrive before 10:00. By midday the sunbeds near the beach club are full.
Walk south to the old Banana Beach Restaurant. Simple Thai food and seafood, fair prices, no loud music.
Bring your own snorkel mask. The beach club rents gear, but it costs more.
Avoid weekends and Thai holidays. The beach is small and fills fast.
In Google Maps the new beach club is 'Banana Beach Club by Sollis 2.0' (10:00-20:00).
items.verification: Checked 15 Oct 2026. Phuket 101 (13 Aug 2026): old path closed late 2025, car park at the north end 100 THB, toilets 20 THB, beach club, old restaurant still open. items.name: Laem Singh Beach

items.bestTime: Morning, when the boulders give shade. Walk in at mid or low tide.
items.openText: Daylight. The boat runs only in good weather.
items.feeText: Free if you walk. Boat 100 THB per person, and the ride back is included (keep the numbered card). About 400 THB to charter the boat.
items.gettingThere: Go to the far south end of Surin Beach. Walk past Tukta Food & Drink (Tukta Restaurant) to the rocks. The path takes 15-20 minutes, with boulders at the start. Or take the small boat from the same spot. No road access since 2017.
items.description: A 300 m cove with golden sand, big granite boulders and clear water, between Surin and Kamala. The road access closed in 2017, so you come by a short boat ride or a rocky walk. Because of this it feels almost empty, even in high season. One small Thai restaurant on the rocks. No sunbeds, shops or toilets.
tips: Wear trainers or sport sandals. The first rocks are slippery.
At high tide take the boat. Waves wash over the low part of the path.
Bring cash. The restaurant takes cash only and there is no ATM nearby.
The best snorkelling is at the south rocks, toward Kamala. Take your rubbish back with you.
items.verification: Checked 15 Oct 2026. Phuket 101 (4 Aug 2026): no road access since April 2017, 15-20 min rock path from the south end of Surin past Tukta, boat 100 THB with free return, charter about 400 THB, one cash-only restaurant, no toilets. items.description: Tiny cove split in two by a small rocky hill, with the island Koh Man in front. Clear water and rocks make it one of the easiest snorkel spots in the south. You can rent kayaks and paddle boards. Two simple Thai restaurants under the trees. It is small, so it can be busy at peak times.
tips: In calm weather, paddle a kayak out toward Koh Man island.
Parking is limited. Come early or use a scooter.
Combine with Summore Day cafe and sunset at Promthep Cape, both a few minutes up the road.

At low tide rocks and coral show, so swim at high tide. Good snorkelling near the rocks. Small cafes with big views sit on the hill road to Paradise Beach.
tips: Wear water shoes. The seabed is rocky.
Blue Harbour Coffee and Sunshine View Restaurant on the hill road have wide views over the bay.
The HideOut Area restaurant is the only place where you eat on the sand.

items.description: Long, quiet bay on the east side of the island, near Cape Panwa. Tall palm trees, a few small beach restaurants and bars, and mostly locals and long-time residents. It still feels like old Phuket. Good for a slow walk, lunch and a swim far from the west-coast crowds.
tips: Akoya Star Lounge, the rooftop bar at V Villas, opens 17:00-23:00 and is busy. Book ahead.
The Cove, a small resort restaurant and bar in the second bay at the east end, sits right by the water.
Combine with the Khao Khad viewpoint tower, about 3 km up the same road.

Bring water and a towel. There are no shops, and little shade outside the restaurant area.
Easy stop on the way to Natai and Phang Nga, just over the bridge.

items.bestTime: Late afternoon. Sunset is about 18:25 in January and it is dark by about 18:50. Start about 1.5 hours before sunset.
items.openText: Open nature area, no gate. Daylight only.

items.gettingThere: From Nai Harn Beach take the road past Ao Sane toward Baan Krating Phuket resort. After the resort an unmarked path goes over rock, grass and scrub to the cape, about 30-35 minutes on foot.
items.description: Wild grassy cape on the south-west coast, west of Nai Harn Beach. After a rough 30-minute walk you get open sea views, big waves on the rocks and Promthep Cape in the distance. It stays quiet. There are no fences, signs or facilities, so it is only for fit walkers in dry weather.
tips: Wear real shoes with grip. Flip-flops do not work here.
Do not go alone, in rain or after dark. The cliff edges have no fence.
Bring water and a torch for the way back.
Ao Sane beach on the route: Phuket 101 (Mar 2026) says it is closed for construction. Check on the spot before you plan a swim.

items.feeText: Free to walk. Food is paid. Community half-day tour from 2,800 THB per person (at least 2 people, book 2-3 days ahead, hotel transfer not included).
items.gettingThere: North-east coast. Coming north on the Pa Khlok road, turn right at the mosque about 1 km north of the Bang Pae Waterfall entrance, and drive to the pier. About 35 km from Patong. Car or scooter. Parking is free if you only eat or look around.
items.description: Small Muslim fishing village on the quiet north-east coast, with the pier for boats to Koh Yao. A wooden boardwalk goes through the mangroves to a floating community restaurant with fresh seafood and views of the boats. Kayaks can be rented to paddle into the mangrove channels; ask ahead.
tips: No alcohol here. This is a Muslim community, so dress modestly.
The community runs half-day tours (pineapple farm, rubber tapping, coconut and cooking). Book at bangrongconnect.com 2-3 days ahead.
Kayak: old reports say about 200 THB per hour at the restaurant. A 2026 guide says to arrange kayaks and boats in advance.
Boats to Koh Yao Noi and Koh Yao Yai leave from this pier.
items.verification: Google: restaurant operational, daily 10:30-18:30, 4.6 from 61 reviews (via Wanderlog, 15 Oct 2026). CBT site live (2026 footer): half day from 2,800 THB, min. 2 people, book 2-3 days ahead, no transfer. Thai Holiday Guide (Jul 2026): free entry, activities arranged in advance. Ferryscanner (2026): boats to Koh Yao Noi and Yai. Directions: Jamie's Phuket Blog.

items.gmapsQuery: The Gibbon Rehabilitation Project, Pa Khlok, Thalang, Phuket
items.bestTime: Morning session (10:30), when the forest is cooler.
items.openText: Visits only in a learning session: 1 hour at 10:30, 12:30 or 14:00, or 2.5 hours 09:30-12:00 (booked on Airbnb). On days with no bookings there are no staff and the project is closed.
items.feeText: 1,100 THB adult when booked online (1,200 THB walk-in), child 5-14 650 THB, under 5 free. Plus national park fee 200 THB adult, 100 THB child, cash only at the gate.
items.gettingThere: At the Bang Pae Waterfall entrance of Khao Phra Thaeo National Park, north-east Phuket, about 20 km from Phuket Town. No hotel pickup: come by car, scooter or taxi.
items.description: Small charity that rescues gibbons from the tourist trade and returns them to the forest. In a one-hour session a guide explains the work at the edge of Phuket's last rainforest. Only 36 visitors a day are allowed, to keep contact with the gibbons low. A calm, honest nature stop.
tips: Book online at least 4 hours before the session. Walk-ins may find it full, or closed if nobody booked.
Bang Pae Waterfall is a short walk away. In January it has less water than in the rainy season (June-November).
A jungle trail links Ton Sai and Bang Pae waterfalls. Do not walk it alone; ask the park rangers about a guide.
Peang Prai, a Thai restaurant at the park entrance listed in the Michelin Guide, is good for lunch.
items.verification: Official booking page and ticket shop (product updated 15 Oct 2026): prices, session times, 36 visitors a day, 4-hour booking cutoff, park fee 200/100 THB cash (fees updated 23 May 2025), 2.5-hour session links to Airbnb. items.name: Koh Sirey: Hilltop Temple and Sea Gypsy Village
items.nameThai: เกาะสิเหร่
items.coordSource: Google pin 'Wat Ban Koh Sirey' (via Wanderlog) + osm temple way 1548196924 + reclining Buddha node 4223066592, within 80 m; village: osm node 11027280955 at 7.8748, 98.4218

items.bestTime: Late afternoon for the view and soft light. Come at lunch time if you want seafood in the village.
items.openText: Temple open in the daytime. The village is a living community, not an attraction.
items.feeText: Free. Leave a small donation if you photograph the reclining Buddha.
items.gettingThere: About 4-5 km east of Phuket Old Town, over a very short bridge, about 15 minutes by car or Grab. A small road climbs to the temple; park and walk up the last part. The Urak Lawoi village is at Laem Tukkae, below the temple to the south-west.
items.description: Small island joined to Phuket Town by a short bridge. On the hilltop, Wat Ban Koh Sirey has a long golden reclining Buddha and a wide view over Phuket Town. Below is Laem Tukkae, a working village of the Urak Lawoi sea people. It is quiet compared with the beach areas. Monkeys live near the bridge.
tips: Cover shoulders and knees in the temple.
In the village, be respectful and ask before you take photos of people.
Keep food and sunglasses away from the monkeys at the bridge.
Hilltop Cafe (a Starbucks) at Sinae Phuket hotel has a 360-degree view, 10:00-20:00. You cannot drive up: buy a 150 THB voucher at the base (it pays for one drink) and take the buggy.
Thai news reported that a landslide damaged the golden-rock shrine at Wat Koh Sirey (late 2025). Ask locally whether it has reopened.

items.name: Wat Phra Thong (Half-Buried Buddha)
items.nameThai: วัดพระทอง
items.coordSource: osm (temple way 319652596) + thaiholidayguide map pin (8.03366, 98.33772), 35 m apart

items.bestTime: Morning, before the heat. Good stop on the way to or from the airport.
items.openText: Daily, about 08:00-17:30.
items.feeText: Free. Donation boxes.
items.gettingThere: In Thalang, central north Phuket, on a side road off Thepkrasattri Road (the main airport road) near the Thalang crossroads. Coming back from the airport, the side road is on your left; signs are poor. About 20 km from Phuket Town. Car, scooter, taxi or Grab.
items.description: Old temple in Thalang with a golden Buddha that comes out of the ground only from the chest up. Local legend says people tried to dig it out but could not. A small museum shows objects from Phuket's tin-mining past. Mostly local people come to pray, so it is calm and real.
tips: Cover shoulders and knees. Take off your shoes in the halls.
Do not touch or take anything from the ground around the buried Buddha. It is sacred.
Wat Phra Nang Sang, one of the oldest temples in Phuket, is about 1 km south-west, on the main road.

items.openText: Mon-Sat 09:00-16:00. Sunday is unclear: Google lists Sun 10:00-16:00 and one 2026 guide says daily, but Phuket 101 (Mar 2026) says closed on Sunday. Call 076 322 137 before a Sunday visit.

items.description: Large air-conditioned museum about the tin mines that made Phuket rich long before tourism. It has a mine tunnel section, a big model mine with many small figures and a rebuilt old Phuket street with Chinese merchant life. Some parts look old and worn. Few foreign visitors come.
tips: Allow 1 to 1.5 hours.
Part of the visit is outside. Bring a hat and water.
Kathu village nearby has old Chinese shrines and is a quiet, local place to walk.

items.openText: Mon-Fri 09:30-11:30 and 13:00-15:30. Free guided tours at 10:30 and 13:30 (45 minutes). Closed Saturday and Sunday.
items.feeText: Free. Donations and shop purchases help the animals.
items.gettingThere: Mai Khao, north Phuket, close to the airport. Address: 167/9 Moo 4, Soi Mai Khao 10. Taxi or car; the website has the address in Thai for drivers.
items.description: Large shelter for street dogs and cats, run by a well-known charity. A free 45-minute guided tour explains their work and introduces some of the 1,800 animals in their care. After the tour you can spend time in the puppy area and the cat house. Tours are in English and Thai.
tips: No booking needed, but arrive on time for the full tour. Outside tour times the tour may be shorter and skip the puppies.
You cannot walk around alone. Stay with the guide.
The puppy area or cat house can close at short notice for quarantine.
Combine with plane spotting at Mai Khao Beach, a few minutes away.
In your dates it is open on weekdays: Fri 8, Mon 11 to Fri 15, Mon 18 to Fri 22, and Mon 25 and Tue 26 January.
Flight day, Tue 26 Jan: the 10:30 tour or the 13:30 tour (ends about 14:15) both fit. The terminal is 15-20 minutes away, so you are there before 15:00.
With luggage, come in a car that waits for you, or first leave your bags at the AIRPORTELs counter in the terminal (150 baht per bag).

items.gettingThere: On the grounds of Wat Karon (Wat Suwan Khiri Khet), Patak Road, about 500 m from the Karon Circle at the back of Karon Beach. Walk from Karon or take a short ride from Kata.

tips: Try the pad thai from the stall at the temple entrance. It is the most famous one.
Bring small cash notes.
Parking is hard. Walk if you stay in Karon, or use the paid car park at the nearby school.
In your dates it runs on Fri 8, Tue 12, Fri 15, Tue 19 and Fri 22 January.

items.gmapsQuery: Khru Vit Seafood Raft, Ko Kaeo, Phuket

items.feeText: Free boat. Most seafood is priced by weight (per 100 g); mid to upper local prices.
items.gettingThere: Drive to Laem Hin Pier, about 10 km north of Phuket Town: take the airport road and turn right onto the small road to Laem Hin. Look for the Kruvit sign. A free longtail boat takes you to the raft in about 5 minutes.
items.description: Big wooden raft restaurant on the sea between Phuket and Koh Maphrao, listed in the 2026 Michelin Guide. Fish, crabs, prawns and oysters live in nets under the deck. You point at what you want and they cook it. Most guests are Thai. A fun and very local seafood meal.
tips: For directions, navigate to Laem Hin Pier (ท่าเรือแหลมหิน), not to the raft. The raft is on the water.
Ask the weight and price before they cook lobster or mantis shrimp.
Try blue crab, grilled king prawns and the sour fish soup with soybean (Pla Tom Towchiew).
Bring cash; cards do not always work on the raft. A 20-50 THB tip for the boatman on the way back is welcome.
Book for weekend evenings. Weekday lunch is usually fine without booking.

items.name: Phang Nga Bay: James Bond Island and sea caves
items.nameThai: อ่าวพังงา เกาะเขาพิงกัน
items.coordSource: wikipedia (Khao Phing Kan) + photon/osm islet way 23492416 + Commons Ko Tapu photo geotag, all within 90 m
items.gmapsQuery: James Bond Island, Phang Nga
items.description: A calm bay full of tall limestone islands. Tours stop at James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan and the Ko Tapu rock), take you by canoe into sea caves and hidden lagoons at Panak or Hong island, and stop for lunch at Koh Panyee, a Muslim fishing village on stilts.
items.feeText: Group tour 1,400-3,500 THB per person: longtail 1,400-1,600, big boat 1,500-1,800, speedboat 1,800-2,500, catamaran or premium 2,500-3,500. Park fee 300 THB (Thai National Parks site, 2022 list) or 400 THB (Phuket 101, 2026); usually included.
items.bestTime: Take an early tour (start 7:00-8:30). Boats crowd the islands 10:00-14:00. December to March is the busiest time.
items.gettingThere: Hotel pickup, then a 45-60 min drive to Ao Po (Ao Por) Pier or Royal Phuket Marina on the east coast. Some longtail tours use Bang Rong Pier. Back at the hotel about 17:00-18:00.
tips: You cannot swim at James Bond Island. Tours stop to swim at other islands.
In the caves a guide paddles the canoe for you. Check that canoeing is included.
At Koh Panyee, walk past the main souvenir walkway to see real village life.
Speedboats spend less time on the water and more time at the islands.
The Hong by Starlight trip also passes James Bond Island (seen from the boat only), so you may not need both.
items.verification: Prices, piers, swim rule and crowd times from Phuket 101 (updated 26 Sep 2026). Park fee conflict: thainationalparks.com (a private site) says 300 THB as of June 2022; Phuket 101 says 400 THB; no 2026 DNP notice found. Coordinates: Wikipedia, OSM and a Commons geotag agree.
items.openText: Tours run daily in the dry season. The park is open in January.

items.name: Hong by Starlight: evening sea-canoe trip
items.nameThai: เกาะห้อง อ่าวพังงา
items.coordSource: wikidata (Ko Hong, Ko Yao district) + photon/osm islet way 23492452 + thaiholidayguide map link, all within 120 m
items.gmapsQuery: Hong Island, Phang Nga Bay, Phang Nga
items.description: John Gray's Sea Canoe runs this trip from midday into the night. You pass James Bond Island (from the boat), then guides paddle you into sea caves and hidden lagoons at Panak and Hong islands. You make a krathong (small floating offering), eat a Thai buffet at sunset, then paddle in the dark to see glowing plankton.
items.feeText: From 3,950 THB per adult (official site). Hotel transfer, light lunch, buffet dinner, park fees and travel insurance are included.
items.openText: Daily. Pickup about 10:20-11:15, back at the hotel about 21:00-21:30.
items.bestTime: Plankton glows best on dark nights. New moon is Fri 8 Jan 2027, so book early in your trip and skip the full-moon days around Fri 22 Jan.
items.gettingThere: Hotel pickup in Phuket. The boat leaves from Ao Po (Ao Por) Pier in north-east Phuket.
tips: The order of stops can change with the tide.
Bring swimwear: there is time to paddle and swim in the afternoon.
A private-charter version of the same trip is sold from 62,750 THB.
Other companies sell similar sunset canoe and plankton trips from about 3,300 THB (for example Tisland 'Shine of Andaman').
items.verification: Official tour page (checked 15 Oct 2026): from 3,950 THB, daily, Ao Po, pickup 10:20-11:15, hotel 21:00-21:30, includes lunch, buffet dinner, park fees, insurance; itinerary passes James Bond Island; private charter from 62,750 THB. items.name: Phi Phi Islands and Maya Bay
items.nameThai: หมู่เกาะพีพี อ่าวมาหยา
items.coordSource: osm (viewpoint node 5314772921 'Maya Bay' on the beach) + about 15 Commons photos geotagged on Maya Bay beach, within 40 m
items.gmapsQuery: Maya Bay, Ko Phi Phi Le, Krabi
items.description: The famous islands 45-60 min by speedboat from Phuket. Tours visit Maya Bay (from the film The Beach), Pileh Lagoon, Viking Cave, snorkel spots and often Bamboo Island. At Maya Bay boats stop at a pier in Loh Samah Bay and you walk in. Swimming is banned there: knee-deep wading only.
items.feeText: Group speedboat tour about 1,500-3,500 THB; sunrise tours 3,500-4,500 THB. Park fee 400 THB (child 200); sometimes not included, so ask. Private speedboat 15,000-25,000 THB per boat.
items.openText: Maya Bay about 07:00-18:00. Closed every year 1 Aug - 30 Sep, so it is open in January.
items.bestTime: Choose an early-departure or sunrise tour to reach Maya Bay before the main crowds.
items.gettingThere: Hotel pickup 6:30-7:30 to Rassada Pier (Phuket Town) or Royal Phuket Marina. Back about 16:00-17:00. Public ferry Rassada - Tonsai about 2 h, about 600 THB one way.
tips: Maya Bay takes up to 375 people per hour. Expect 30-60 minutes on the beach.
Sunscreen with oxybenzone, octinoxate, 4MBC or butylparaben is banned in Thai national parks (fines up to 100,000 THB).
For seasickness, take a pill 30 minutes before and sit at the back of the boat.
If you stay a night on Phi Phi Don, the last ferry back to Phuket is about 15:30.
items.verification: Tisland blog (28 Sep 2026): Maya Bay reopened 1 Oct 2026 after the 1 Aug - 30 Sep closure, 07:00-18:00, 375 people per hour, knee-deep wading only, Loh Samah pontoon, fee 400/200 THB, sunscreen ban. Phuket 101 (12 Apr 2026): tour, private boat and ferry prices, 30-45 min on the beach. Tisland lists Phi Phi tours from 1,900 THB (Oct 2026).

items.name: Similan Islands
items.nameThai: หมู่เกาะสิมิลัน
items.coordSource: osm beach 'Ao Kueak' (= Donald Duck Bay, Island 8) + google maps 'Donald Duck Bay', 24 m apart; Sail Rock viewpoint node 180 m north
items.gmapsQuery: Donald Duck Bay, Similan Islands, Phang Nga
items.description: A national park of granite islands about 60 km off the Khao Lak coast, with the clearest water and best snorkelling near Phuket. You climb Sail Rock on Island 8 for the famous view of Donald Duck Bay, snorkel between islands and have lunch on Island 4. Open 15 Oct 2026 to 15 May 2027.
items.feeText: Day tour from Phuket about 2,500-3,800 THB with transfer, lunch and park fee. Park fee alone: 500 THB (child 250), as an e-ticket.
items.openText: Season 15 Oct 2026 - 15 May 2027. Day visits only: no overnight stays.
items.bestTime: January is ideal for sea and sun but very busy. Take an early-departure tour.
items.gettingThere: Long day. Hotel pickup about 06:00-07:00 (early tours 03:00-04:30), then 1-1.5 h by van to Thap Lamu Pier (Khao Lak) and 60-90 min by speedboat. Back in Phuket in the evening.
tips: Only 3,325 day visitors (plus 525 divers) are allowed per day, shared by all tour companies. Book ahead.
Avoid the cheapest speedboats: they are crowded. Mid-range boats have shade and space.
Do not feed fish and do not stand on coral.
The ride is much shorter if you stay in Khao Lak.
items.verification: Season 15 Oct 2026 - 15 May 2027 confirmed by Naewna (Thai news, 13 Oct 2026), Tisland blog (21 Sep 2026) and Phuket 101 (14 Oct 2026). Fee 500/250 THB and e-ticket from Tisland and Phuket 101. Quota: 3,850 total = 3,325 day visitors + 525 divers (Tisland 2026; 2018-2020 news). items.nameThai: เกาะราชาใหญ่

items.description: A hilly island 30-45 min by speedboat south of Phuket, with white sand and very clear water. Day boats land at Patok Bay, where you can snorkel straight from the beach. A short walk leads to quieter Siam Bay. Many tours combine Racha with Coral Island.
items.feeText: Racha + Coral speedboat tour from about 1,300 THB per person with lunch. No national park fee.
items.bestTime: November to April has calm sea and clear water. Day boats arrive from about 10:00. The island empties around 16:00.
items.gettingThere: Hotel pickup 7:00-9:00 to Chalong Pier, then speedboat 30-45 min (big boats 60-90 min). Back at the pier about 15:30-16:30.
tips: Bring a towel: Patok Bay has no public sunbeds.
Bring your own mask if you have one. Rental masks often leak.
Stay a night at a Patok Bay resort to have the beach almost to yourself after 16:00.
Divers: manta rays pass Racha Noi from January to March.

items.name: Coral Island (Koh Hey)
items.nameThai: เกาะเฮ

items.gmapsQuery: Coral Island (Koh Hey), Phuket
items.description: A small island only 15 min by speedboat from Chalong or Rawai. Most boats land at busy Long Beach with restaurants, sunbeds and water sports. Banana Beach, further east, is quieter and is mostly visited with its own day packages. Easy snorkelling near the shore. A short and cheap escape.
items.feeText: Free entry. Speedboat tour with lunch 1,100-2,200 THB per person. Banana Beach packages from 1,900 THB. Longtail from Rawai 1,500-2,000 THB per boat. Sunbeds and water sports cost extra.
items.bestTime: November to April has the calmest water. Long Beach is busiest from late morning to early afternoon.
items.gettingThere: Speedboat from Chalong Pier or Rawai Beach (about 15 min), or a shared or private longtail from Rawai.
tips: For a quieter beach, book a boat or package that lands at Banana Beach.
Often sold together with Racha Yai as one full-day trip.
items.verification: Thai Holiday Guide (Jul 2026): free entry, 15 min crossing, tour and longtail prices, Long Beach busiest late morning. Tisland from 1,100 THB (Oct 2026). Banana Beach packages 1,900-3,300 THB on its official site (2026). No source and no OSM path confirm a walk between the beaches, so that tip was removed. Coords: OSM + Google agree.

items.name: Khai Islands (Koh Khai Nok)
items.nameThai: เกาะไข่นอก
items.coordSource: wikidata (Ko Khai Nok) + photon/osm + google maps 'Koh Khai Nok' (31 m), all within 120 m
items.gmapsQuery: Koh Khai Nok, Phang Nga
items.description: Three tiny islands 15-20 min by speedboat from Phuket's east coast. Khai Nok has a white beach with bars and sunbeds. Khai Nai is the largest, with long, shallow sand. Khai Nui has no beach but the best reef: you snorkel from the boat. Short, easy and cheap, but always busy.
items.feeText: Half-day speedboat tour about 1,100 THB (child 900), with transfer, snorkel gear and entry fees. Full day with another island about 1,250 THB. Private speedboat 2,500-5,000 THB. Sunbeds 150 THB for two, free with a food order.
items.bestTime: Leave early in the morning, before the tour groups. November to April is calmest.
items.gettingThere: Hotel pickup to Chalong Pier, Ao Po Pier or Royal Phuket Marina, then 15-20 min by speedboat.
tips: Feeding fish is banned. Rangers give fines.
Keep your life jacket on at Khai Nui: the current can be strong.
Boats skip Khai Nui when the sea is rough.
items.verification: Phuket 101 (updated 29 Aug 2026) for prices, sunbeds, fish-feeding ban and Khai Nui current. No closure news found in English or Thai searches (Oct 2026); Google listing active (1,329 reviews). Coords: Wikidata, OSM and Google agree. items.name: Koh Yao Noi
items.nameThai: เกาะยาวน้อย
items.coordSource: wikidata + osm island relation label point, 60 m apart (island centre). Google's island pin is 2.5 km south-west; Manoh Pier (arrival) is at 8.0935, 98.5872 (osm + google, 15 m)
items.gmapsQuery: Koh Yao Noi, Phang Nga
items.description: A quiet, green island in Phang Nga Bay, 30 min by speedboat from Phuket. Rent a scooter, ride past rice fields and small villages, swim at Pasai or Klong Jark beach and kayak to Koh Nok. Views over the limestone islands of the bay. Mostly Muslim and not a party island: a real break.
items.feeText: Speedboat about 300-500 THB per person each way (price differs by seller and online). Slow longtail about 300 THB. Scooter 250-350 THB a day. Kayak about 300 THB for a few hours.
items.openText: Speedboats from Bang Rong Pier about 08:40-17:00 (longtail 12:30). Boats back from Manoh Pier about 06:35-16:00: the last one is about 16:00.
items.bestTime: Take the first boat (08:40). Better: stay one or two nights.
items.gettingThere: Grab or taxi to Bang Rong Pier (north-east Phuket, about 22 km and 40 min from the airport). Speedboat 30-40 min, or the slow longtail at 12:30 (1 h), to Manoh Pier. Taxis and songthaews wait at the pier.
tips: Dress modestly in the villages. Not every shop sells alcohol.
Kayak to Koh Nok early, at high tide. The afternoon sea is choppy.
Koh Hong (Krabi) is about 20 min by longtail from Klong Jark Beach (about 800 THB per person in 2024).
Bring enough cash. ATMs can run out on busy weekends.
Phuket 101 says two nights is the minimum to enjoy the island.
items.verification: Phuket 101 (27 Aug 2026): about 300 THB, first boat 08:40, last 17:00, longtail 12:30, scooter and kayak prices, ATM tip. Camphadee timetable (Nov 2025): speedboat 400 THB, longtail 300, last boat from Manoh 16:00. Ferryscanner (Sep 2026): Manoh departures 06:35-16:00, EUR 8.70-12.27. Siamtickets lists 400-500 THB. Drive time by OSRM.

items.name: Koh Hong (Krabi): lagoon island
items.nameThai: เกาะห้อง กระบี่
items.coordSource: wikidata (Ko Hong, Krabi) + google maps 'Ko Hong' island (63 m) and 'Hong Lagoon' (65 m); Commons lagoon photo GPS within 120 m
items.gmapsQuery: Hong Island, Krabi
items.description: A limestone island between Koh Yao Noi and Krabi. Boats go into a shallow lagoon ringed by tall cliffs, and there are two white-sand beaches with clear water. Steep stairs lead to a viewpoint. It is part of a national park and is busy from late morning.
items.feeText: Park fee 300 THB per adult, cash, paid at the floating pier. From Koh Yao Noi: longtail about 800 THB per person (2024). From Krabi or Ao Nang: group speedboat tours about 1,350-1,500 THB.
items.bestTime: Go early. Tour boats from Krabi arrive in the late morning.
items.gettingThere: From Phuket, some speedboat island tours include Hong (Krabi); ask for it by name. Or stay on Koh Yao Noi and take a longtail (about 20 min) from Klong Jark Beach.
tips: No alcohol and no drones on the island.
Expect a long, bouncy floating pier to reach the beach.
Koh Pakbia, nearby, is a good picnic stop.
Do not mix it up with Koh Hong in Phang Nga Bay (Hong by Starlight trip).

items.name: Railay Beach (Krabi)
items.nameThai: ไร่เลย์
items.coordSource: osm West Railay beach relation centre (nominatim) + google maps 'Railay Beach' (19 m); google 'Railay West Beach' pin is 200 m north on the same beach
items.gmapsQuery: Railay Beach West, Krabi
items.description: A beach area in Krabi with no roads, closed in by huge limestone cliffs, so you arrive by boat. West Railay is a beautiful sunset beach and Phra Nang Cave Beach is close by. Famous for rock climbing. A direct ferry from Phuket makes a long day trip possible, but one or two nights is better.
items.feeText: Ferry Phuket - Railay about 660-1,360 THB one way (EUR 17.65-36 online, Oct 2026).
items.openText: Ferries leave Rassada Pier 08:30-12:00 (1 h 20 min - 2 h 30 min). Back from Railay 12:45-15:15.
items.bestTime: For a day trip take the first ferry. If you stay, watch sunset at West Railay (about 18:25 in mid-January).
items.gettingThere: Ferry from Rassada Pier (Phuket Town) to Railay East floating pier, then a short walk to West Railay. Longtails link Railay with Ao Nang and Krabi Town.
tips: Book the ferry early: online prices rise close to the date.
Be at the pier 60 minutes before departure.
There are no night ferries back to Phuket.

items.name: Khao Sok: Cheow Lan Lake overnight
items.nameThai: เขื่อนเชี่ยวหลาน
items.coordSource: google maps 'Ratchaprapha Marina' + 'Cheow Lan Pier (Ratchaprapha Pier)' + osm pier ways, within 80 m. Old pin (dam viewpoint) was 1.6 km west of the boat pier
items.gmapsQuery: Cheow Lan Pier (Ratchaprapha Pier), Ban Ta Khun, Surat Thani
items.description: A huge jungle lake with limestone cliffs in Khao Sok National Park. Longtail boats take you from the dam pier to floating raft houses. You sleep on the water, swim, and kayak in the morning mist. A 1-day tour exists but is very long (about 15 hours), so one night is better.
items.feeText: 1-day tour from Phuket from 3,500 THB; 2 days / 1 night from 7,900 THB (park fees included). Lake fee alone: 300 THB (child 150).
items.openText: Boats run only between sunrise and sunset.
items.bestTime: January to March is the dry season.
items.gettingThere: Tour pickup in Phuket 05:00-06:30. The 1-day tour reaches the lake about 10:00 and is back about 19:30-20:30. The pier is about 155 km by road from Phuket Airport (about 3 h). All boats leave from Ratchaprapha Pier at the dam.
tips: Some raft houses are up to 1 h 20 min by boat from the pier.
Basic raft houses often have power only in the evening.
Boats are limited in high season, so book ahead.
On the lake, mobile signal works mainly on AIS.
items.verification: thainationalparks.com (fees as of June 2026): lake 300/150 THB, boats only sunrise-sunset, raft houses up to 1 h 20 min, evening power, AIS signal, boat shortages into 2026. Tisland (Oct 2026): 1-day 3,500 THB, pickup 05:00-06:30, lake 10:00, back 19:30-20:30; 2D1N 7,900 THB. Road distance by OSRM. Pin moved to the boat pier (Google + OSM).

items.name: Samet Nangshe viewpoint (sunrise)
items.nameThai: จุดชมวิวเสม็ดนางชี
items.coordSource: osm viewpoint node + Commons photo GPS (13 Apr 2026) + second google listing 'Samet Nangshe Viewpoint' (40 m). The main google listing pins the car park / truck stop 860 m south-east
items.gmapsQuery: Samet Nangshe Viewpoint, Takua Thung, Phang Nga
items.description: A hilltop viewpoint over Phang Nga Bay: green mangroves and dozens of limestone islands in the morning mist. Come for sunrise. From the car park you walk up about 20 minutes or take a pickup truck. There are two viewpoints on the way up.
items.feeText: 30 THB on foot, 90 THB return by pickup truck (entry included). Sunrise tour from Phuket about 2,200-2,400 THB.
items.openText: Opens about 05:00-05:30 every day.
items.bestTime: Arrive by 05:30-06:00. Sunrise in January is about 06:45; the sky gets light from about 06:20.
items.gettingThere: About 50 km (1 h) by car from Phuket Airport, about 80 km (1.5-2 h) from Patong. Cross the Sarasin Bridge and drive north to Takua Thung. Sunrise tours pick up about 04:00.
tips: Private cars must stop at the bottom car park. Google Maps' main pin is this car park and truck stop.
Wear real shoes and bring water. The path is steep and has no shade.
Sleep at the top in a tent (about 130 THB) or a bungalow (500-700 THB) to skip the night drive.
The small platforms fill up fast on clear mornings, especially at weekends.
items.verification: Fees 30/90 THB: Thai Holiday Guide (Jul 2026) and Phuket 101 (Mar 2026) agree; opening 05:00 or 05:30. Two viewpoints about 800 m apart (Thai Holiday Guide); no source says which is better, so that claim was removed. Tour from 2,400 THB, pickup about 04:00 (Tisland, Oct 2026). Sunrise computed: 06:43-06:45. Distances by OSRM.

items.name: Koh Phangan rave trip (2-5 days)
items.nameThai: เกาะพะงัน
items.coordSource: google maps 'OXA - Jungle Party' (address 72/52 Moo 2 Ban Tai matches Megatix). Halfmoon Magic Forest is 480 m south-west (osm + google). Old pin was on Ban Tai beach, 2.3 km south of the party area
items.gmapsQuery: OXA - Jungle Party, Ban Tai, Koh Phangan
items.description: Thailand's party island, in the Gulf. Most jungle raves are inland near Ban Tai. With the group: OXA (Fri 8 and 15 Jan), Lost Jungle psytrance (Sat 9 to Mon 11) and Halfmoon (Fri 15 - Sat 16). In full-moon week: OXA (Tue 19), Waterfall (Wed 20), Jungle Experience (Thu 21) and the Full Moon Party (Fri 22 Jan).
items.feeText: Flight Phuket - Samui about 3,000 to 5,000 THB one way, plus the boat. Bus + boat about 700-1,600 THB. Party tickets: OXA from 500 THB; Halfmoon about 1,500-3,500 THB at the gate (online often a bit less).
items.bestTime: Two good windows. With the group: Sun 10 to Wed 13 Jan (Lost Jungle until 11 Jan, Chill Up on Mon 11, the Lighthouse Party on Tue 12). For the two of you: Tue 19 to Sat 23 Jan, the full-moon week, then fly back for the last Circoloco on Sat 23. See Info, Koh Phangan full-moon week.
items.gettingThere: Fastest: Bangkok Airways Phuket - Koh Samui (about 1 h, 8 flights a day; take one at 14:15 or earlier to catch the boats), then a 20-60 min boat (Lomprayah or Seatran) to Thong Sala Pier. Budget: bus + boat via Don Sak, about 6-9 h (Lomprayah 07:00-12:45 or 09:30-16:30 in Oct 2026).
tips: Bring cash. Party bars are cash only and OXA has no ATM.
Bring your passport: Halfmoon checks ID, and some ticket sites say 20+.
Eden Garden on Haad Yuan has deep house and techno on Saturdays. Taxi boat from Haad Rin about 400 THB.
Night taxis charge per car, so share a ride.
Small underground nights post dates only 1-3 weeks ahead. Check RA and phangan.events in December.
Full-moon week (20-24 Jan): rooms cost 2-3 times more and many ask for a 3-5 night minimum. Book in October or November. Ban Tai is the best base.
items.verification: Halfmoon official 2027 chart: beach party Fri 15 Jan (14:00-24:00), main night Sat 16 Jan (from 21:30). OXA Fri 8 and Fri 15 Jan, 21:00-05:00, from 500 THB, cash only (Megatix). Lost Jungle Sat 9 12:00 - Tue 12 Jan 06:00 (phangan.events). Circoloco 9, 16, 23 Jan (EDM House Network, Aug 2026). Halfmoon prices: Thai Holiday Guide (Oct 2026). Transport: Direct Ferries and Cheapflights (Oct 2026). Full Moon 22 Jan is a projected date.

items.description: Phuket family recipes in an old Old Town shophouse with vintage decor. Order the crab meat yellow curry with rice noodles, moo hong (sweet braised pork belly) and fried prawns in tamarind sauce. Michelin Bib Gourmand 2026.
items.feeText: Dishes about 120-390 THB (crab curry 390, moo hong 265; 2024 menu).
items.openText: 10:00-22:00 daily (Tue until 21:00).
items.bestTime: Lunch, then walk around the Old Town.
tips: Raya, the famous older restaurant with the same Phuket dishes, is a few steps away at 48/1 Dibuk Road (Google lists 11:00-21:00). Its main rooms have no air-con, and it left the Michelin guide in 2026.
Ask for less spicy if you are not used to Thai chili.

items.description: Phuket's best-known Hokkien noodle shop, cooking since 1946 at the clock tower circle in Phuket Town. The classic is mee Hokkien: thick yellow noodles fried with pork, seafood and greens in a rich gravy, topped with a soft egg. Add pork satay. Simple, fast and cheap.
items.feeText: Cheap: mee Hokkien with egg about 80 THB, Phuket fish balls 80 THB, hor mok 20 THB (Wongnai review, Mar 2026).
items.openText: Phuket Town shop 09:30-18:30 daily.
items.bestTime: Breakfast or lunch.
tips: One plate is usually enough. Order a second if you are hungry.
The shop next door serves the same noodles as a soup.
Other branches: Mee Ton Poe 2 in Kathu and Mee Ton Poe 4 on Thep Krasattri Road in Thalang (both open until about 20:00).

items.description: A corner shop open at night, known for kuay jap (rolled rice noodles in peppery pork broth) and khao tom (rice soup), with crispy pork belly on the side. Open until about 1:30 at night, so it is perfect after a party. Michelin Bib Gourmand every year since 2019.
items.feeText: Dishes 50-90 THB (rice soup or kuay jap 50, crispy pork 60-90). Drinks 20 THB. Cash only.
items.openText: Tue-Sun 17:00-01:30. Closed Mon and on Buddhist holy days (in your dates: Fri 15 and Fri 22 Jan).
items.bestTime: Peak is 19:00-21:00 with a 20-30 min queue. Quieter after 21:30 and after midnight.
tips: Take any free seat; staff come to take your order.
The dry rice soup with crispy pork and offal often sells out.
Parking is hard. Come by Grab or taxi.
items.verification: Michelin page data: Bib Gourmand 2026, 163 Krabi Rd. Google hours (fetched 15 Oct 2026): Tue-Sun 17:00-01:30, Mon closed. items.name: Mor Mu Dong (mangrove seafood)
items.nameThai: หมอมูดง
items.coordSource: google maps place pin (7.84309, 98.37201) + michelin page geo + osm node, all within 10 m
items.gmapsQuery: Mor Mu Dong Restaurant, Chalong, Phuket
items.description: Southern Thai food in open wooden huts over a mangrove canal near Chalong, about 10 km from Phuket Town. Mostly local diners. Live seafood waits in tanks by the open kitchen. Try stuffed mackerel, salt-fried pork, sea grape salad, lime squid and salt-crusted fish. Michelin Bib Gourmand.
items.feeText: Most dishes 100-200 THB; whole fish by weight. About 300-500 THB per person. Cards are listed as accepted, but bring cash as backup.
items.openText: Daily 10:00-21:00. Closed on the 15th of every month (on your trip: Fri 15 Jan).
items.bestTime: Weekdays are calmer. On weekends arrive before 12:00: the car park fills and you take a queue number. High tide gives the best view (check a tide app). At low tide you see mud and small red crabs.
tips: Order the salt-crusted fish (pla pao) first. It takes about 30 minutes.
No reservations. On busy days you take a number and wait. Ask for a hut over the water.
In the huts you sit on the floor at a low table. Some bigger huts, and the tables under the trees, have chairs.
The menu has photos of every dish, so you can point.
Backup on the 15th or when it is full: Chaiyo Seafood Restaurant (daily 10:30-21:30). It is across the canal, but about 10 km by road.
items.verification: Checked 15 Oct 2026. Google Maps 'Mor Mu Dong Restaurant': operating, daily 10:00-21:00, 3,753 reviews. Michelin site: same hours, and its Phuket Bib Gourmand list (18 places) includes it. Closed on the 15th: Phuket 101 (30 Sep 2026) and Wongnai agree. Coords: Google pin, Michelin geo and OSM node within 10 m. Chaiyo: Google/OSM pin 480 m north across the canal, 9.6 km by road (OSRM).
items.gettingThere: Car, scooter or Grab. About 20-25 min from Phuket Town (10 km), 25-30 min from Kata (11 km) and 35-45 min from Patong (20 km). It is at the end of a small road in the mangroves. Google Maps finds it easily.

items.name: Malin Plaza night market (Patong)
items.nameThai: มาลิน พลาซ่า
items.coordSource: google maps place pin (7.88264, 98.29318) + osm marketplace polygon (edited Sep 2026), 80 m apart
items.gmapsQuery: Malin Plaza, Prachanukhro Rd, Patong, Phuket
items.description: A big covered night market at the south end of Patong. The front half is food: grills, seafood on ice that they cook for you, pad thai, fruit, pancakes and mango sticky rice, with shared tables. The back half sells clothes and souvenirs. Touristy and warm (no air-con), but cheap for Patong.
items.feeText: Free entry. Street dishes about 80-120 THB (pad thai 80, pad kra pao 100-120). Seafood is by weight: ask the total before they cook it.
items.openText: Daily 11:00-23:00. Almost empty until late afternoon.
items.bestTime: 18:00-19:00: stalls are ready and tables are free. Busiest 20:00-22:00, peak around 21:00.
tips: Bargain for souvenirs, not for food. A cap offered at 250 THB sold for 70 THB.
Look at a few food stalls first: a few charge more than the others.
Halal food: several stalls show it on the sign. Check each stall.
Some sellers in the shopping half are pushy. A smile and a 'no' works.
items.verification: Checked 15 Oct 2026. Google Maps 'Malin Plaza' (night market): operating, daily 11:00-23:00, 8,997 reviews. Phuket 101 (12 Aug 2026): same hours, free entry, 2025-2026 prices, layout, tuk-tuk 200 THB, 1.6 km from Bangla Road. No closure news in English or Thai search. Coords: Google pin; OSM marketplace polygon 80 m away. Bangla Road to market 1.5 km by road (OSRM).
items.gettingThere: South end of Patong on Prachanukhro Road, 1.6 km from Bangla Road (about 20 minutes on foot). Tuk-tuk from central or north Patong about 200 THB, or use Grab. Parking is hard: a scooter is fine, a car is not.

items.bestTime: Morning for calm water and space. Late afternoon for a long walk and sunset (about 18:25).
items.openText: Always open.
items.feeText: Free.
items.gettingThere: In Karon you walk to the sand. From Patong about 15 min over the hill road, from Kamala about 30-40 min, by car, scooter or Grab. Kata is next door to the south.
items.description: A wide 3 km beach of soft, pale sand between Patong and Kata. Most hotels are across the beach road, so the sand rarely feels crowded. From December to April the sea is usually calm for swimming. The dry sand squeaks under your feet. Good for long walks at sunset.
tips: Always check the flags. Rip currents are mainly a May-October problem, but they can still happen.
The north end is the quietest part. After heavy rain, dark water from the canal near Nong Harn lake can run across the sand there. Swim away from it.
The south end, near Kata, has TANN Beach Club (11:00-23:00) with a fire show every night at about 19:00.
Karon Temple Market runs Tuesday and Friday, 16:00-22:00, at Wat Karon, about 10 minutes on foot from the middle of the beach.
Jet skis and parasailing work off the sand in high season. Swim away from them.

items.description: About 2 km of soft, pale sand with shade trees. The quiet town behind it grew from a Muslim fishing village. It is the base suggested in this guide. In the high season the sea is shallow, calm and clear, one of the easiest swims on the island. Small Thai restaurants and bamboo bars sit on the sand, good for sunset.

items.bestTime: Morning, for the clearest water and shade under the trees. Or late afternoon for sunset (about 18:25).
items.openText: Always open.
items.feeText: Free. In early 2026 there were no sunbeds or umbrellas for rent.
items.gettingThere: About 5-10 min north of Kamala by car, scooter or Grab. About 20 min from Patong.
items.description: An 800 m bay of soft, pale sand with casuarina trees for shade, 5-10 minutes north of Kamala. Between 2023 and May 2025 the bars, sunbeds and beach massage were removed from the sand, so it looks natural again. From December to April the water is often clear and calm: some of the best swimming on the island.
tips: Bring a towel or mat. In early 2026 visitors found no sunbeds or umbrellas to rent. Food and drinks are sold at stalls by the car park and in cafes across the road.
Eat at Tukta Food & Drink, on the rocks at the south end (10:30-21:00). The stairs to the upper floors are hidden, but the view is worth it.
From the south end, walk 15-20 min over the rocks (easier at mid to low tide), or take the 100 THB boat, to Laem Singh Beach. The boat may not run in bad weather.
In the low season (May-October) the sea can be rough. In January it is usually calm, but some visitors report deep water and currents a few metres out. Check the flags.

items.bestTime: Late morning to about 14:00, when more planes land. Low tide gives a wider beach for photos. From December to June most planes land over the sea. On your flight day, Tue 26 Jan, come about 11:00-13:30.
items.openText: Open beach. Planes land all day.
items.feeText: Free. Motorbike ride from the car park to the runway end: 20 THB. If you come in through Sirinat National Park from the Nai Yang side, the park fee can apply (200 THB per foreign adult in 2026).
items.gettingThere: Drive north past the airport and follow the signs with a plane picture to the car park by the beach. Walk about 500 m south on the sand to the end of the runway, or take a 20 THB motorbike ride. About 20 min from the terminal (the road goes around the runway), 40-50 min from Kamala, about 60 min from Patong.
items.description: At the south end of Mai Khao Beach, planes pass very low over your head just before they land at Phuket Airport. In the high season the wind comes from the east, so most planes come in over the sea and the sand. It is loud, a little crazy and free. Drink and food stalls wait at the car park and the runway end.
tips: Open the FlightRadar24 app to see when the next plane lands. Planes that come in from the west, over the sea, pass over the beach.
Watch from the side. Standing in the landing path is not allowed, and jet blast from planes waiting to take off throws sand hard.
If the wind is from the west, planes land from the other side and only take-offs pass over the beach. In January the wind is usually from the east.
Do not fly a drone. The beach is next to the runway, in the airport no-fly zone.
Bring a cap and water. There is no shade on the sand.
Good last stop on Tue 26 Jan: watch until about 13:30-14:00, walk back to the car park, then drive about 20 minutes around the runway to the terminal (be there by 15:20).
With luggage on the last day, come with a driver who waits for you, or first leave your bags at the AIRPORTELs counter in the terminal (150 baht per bag).
